stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan brews over Bay of Bengal: What you need to know
stories.deck: Cyclone Akvan may intensify into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal by Tuesday (November 17, 2026)
stories.bodyText:
A weather system brewing over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm on Monday evening (November 16, 2026), according to the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD).
It is moving north-northwestwards towards Andhra Pradesh at 10 kmph and has been named ‘Akvan’, a name suggested by Iran under the North Indian Ocean naming list.
What is Cyclone Akvan’s current trajectory?
It originated as a well-marked low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal on Saturday (November 14, 2026), the system intensified into a depression by Sunday (November 15, 2026) morning.
The storm may continue to move north-northwestwards and intensify into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal by Tuesday (November 17, 2026) evening and may cross the A.P. coast around noon on November 20, as a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm, with windspeed gusting to 145 kmph, similar to that of Arnab. The system is forecast to bypass Tamil Nadu and move toward the Andhra Pradesh coast around November 19, 2026, also impacting Odisha.
ALSO WATCH Odisha braces for possible third cyclone in three weeks as Bay of Bengal system intensifies
Rainfall alerts across States
Heavy rainfall warnings have been issued for coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Andaman and Nicobar Islands through November 20, 2026. In West Bengal, heavy rain is forecast for South 24 Parganas and Purba Medinipur from November 19 to 21, 2026, with downpour likely in the southern districts of Howrah, Paschim Medinipur and Jhargram on November 20 and 21.
According to the IMD, thunderstorms, accompanied with winds up to 40 kmph in Kolkata and most districts of Gangetic West Bengal is also likely.
Also read: How are tropical cyclones named?
A nip in the air over South Bengal is likely to dissipate as day and night temperatures will rise by two to three degrees Celsius from November 18, 2026, it said.
Cyclone Akvan is expected to cause rains in north coastal districts in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal area, it said.
Unusual weather patterns
Along the north Andhra coast, at Visakhapatnam Fishing Harbour, the Fisheries Department and Indian Coast Guard have recalled trawlers and halted marine operations.
Andhra Pradesh already endured Cyclone Arnab in late October and Murasu this November, local boat crews face mounting tension and loss of of wages as they secure vessels against these adverse conditions. According to Regional Meteorological Centre officials, the formation of three cyclones within a single month is unusual and maybe linked to a strong El Niño and warm sea surface temperatures that may be triggering these disturbances.
Published - November 17, 2026 06:57 am IST

briefs.headline: Census 2027 turning out to be farce: Congress
briefs.deck: Census 2027 is turning out to be a farce in many respects. This will have grave implications, Jairam Ramesh said
briefs.bodyText:
The Congress on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) claimed that the Census 2027 is turning out to be a "farce" in many respects, and this will have "grave implications".
Congress general secretary in charge of communications Jairam Ramesh shared a media report on X that claimed that ISKCON, Ramakrishna Paramahamsa, Sanatan, Shri Ram, Shri Krishna, Balmiki, Ramdev, Sufi, Shia, Sunni, Methodist, Pentecostal, etc. were listed among 287 "other" religions on the Census self-enumeration portal, but soon after a query was raised with the Home Ministry, the list was quietly removed from the portal without an explanation.
In his post, Mr. Ramesh said, "This is bizarre and defies any understanding. And where the drop-down menu should be provided, for instance, for castes other than scheduled castes and scheduled tribes, it is not."
"Census 2027 is turning out to be a farce in many respects. This will have grave implications," the Congress leader said.
The Congress has in the past accused the government of turning Census 2027 into a process with a "very dubious" intent, raising concerns over the quality and purpose of the data to be collected.
Earlier, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi had jointly written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the caste census issue, setting out the party's key demand for the exercise to be conducted in the right manner.

BJP calls Sonia Gandhi’s memoir launch a ‘self-goal’, says it exposes Congress’ past misdeeds
briefs.deck: The memoir and the timing of its release, just ahead of state Assembly elections, reek of political opportunism, he said
briefs.bodyText:
The BJP has criticised the launch of Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi's memoir, alleging that it was an attempt to sanitise the party's past wrongdoings and give the Nehru-Gandhi family a "clean chit".
Talking to PTI Videos, BJP national spokesperson C.R. Kesavan said the memoir launch was a "highly damaging self-goal" from the perspective of the younger generation, as it had exposed the Congress' "dark misrule and past misdeeds", including the "cold-blooded" 1984 anti-Sikh massacre and the Emergency.
"While a personal memoir is entitled to reflect an individual's viewpoint, Sonia Gandhi's memoir appears to be a calculated attempt to sanitise the political wrongdoings for which the Congress, led by the Nehru-Gandhi family, is solely responsible," he said.
Mr. Kesavan also questioned the timing of the memoir's release, alleging that it was politically motivated as it came ahead of the state Assembly elections.
"The memoir and the timing of its release, just ahead of state Assembly elections, reek of political opportunism," he said.
"The memoir's futile attempt to somehow give a clean chit to the Congress first family by distorting, omitting and varnishing historical facts has spectacularly backfired, and this is very evident from the widespread criticism and backlash this memoir continues to receive," he said.
"Belonging: A journey of Love", written by Sonia Gandhi, was formally launched by her with her children, Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, standing by her side at a function in the presence of several leaders of the INDIA opposition bloc, Chief Ministers of Congress-ruled states and top leaders of the party, besides Bharatiya Janata Party leader and former Punjab Chief Minister Amarinder Singh.
Several INDIA bloc leaders, including SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and TMC's Abhishek Banerjee, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and BJP leader Amarinder Singh, attended the launch of Sonia Gandhi's memoir.
The book, published by HarperCollins India, was released on November 10.

briefs.headline: Nikhara drive: Cases registered against 275 traders for cheating on weights in Karnataka
briefs.deck: Following complaints that farmers were being cheated through manipulation of weights, over 100 officials inspected agricultural produce markets in Bengaluru, Mysuru, Gangavathi, Raichur, Tumakuru, Hubballi, and Byadagi
briefs.bodyText:
Continuing the ‘Nikhara’ drive, officials from the Department of Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs, and Legal Metrology conducted simultaneous inspections across nine major Agricultural Produce Markets (APMCs) in the State on Monday morning.
They registered cases against 275 traders for cheating on weights and violating standards set by the Legal Metrology Department, imposing fines totalling ₹9.6 lakh, according to a release from the department. Minister for Food, Civil Supplies, and Consumer Affairs Rizwan Arshad led the inspection at the Bandipalya APMC in Mysuru.
Following complaints that farmers were being cheated through the manipulation of weights of agricultural produce, over 100 officials and staff from the Legal Metrology division launched simultaneous inspections at 6 a.m. in the agricultural produce markets of Bengaluru, Mysuru, Gangavathi, Raichur, Tumakuru, Hubballi and Byadagi. The inspections continued until 1 p.m., the release said.
In addition to imposing fines totalling ₹9,61,000 on these traders, department officials confiscated the faulty weighing equipment along with weights that had not undergone the mandatory verification and stamping process.
Furthermore, the Minister instructed officials to ensure that a ‘reference’ weighing machine, provided by the Department of Legal Metrology, was installed in every market across the State.

stories.headline: SIR: No application records for over 1.13 lakh new enrolments in Bengaluru’s final voter rolls
stories.deck: An analysis of the final rolls across Bengaluru’s 28 Assembly constituencies finds that 44% of new enrolments cannot be matched to Form 6 or Form 8 records – the two ways through which a voter is enrolled
stories.bodyText:
Across Bengaluru’s 28 Assembly constituencies, at least 1,13,059 new enrolments added to the final electoral rolls after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) could not be traced, an analysis by The Hindu has found. These additions, which could not be traced, account for approximately 44% of the 2,55,926 new enrolments in the final rolls, nearly one in every two new enrolments.
Additions to the final electoral rolls after the SIR were made through two routes: Form 6, used by people seeking to enroll as “new voters”, and Form 8, which was used during polling-station rationalisation to shift existing voters from one polling station to another within the same or different Assembly constituency.
During the SIR, the Election Commission capped the number of electors at each polling station at 1,200. Consequently, where a polling station exceeded this limit, some voters had to be shifted to another polling station. These changes were made through Form 8 and therefore names were added within or outside the constituency. On the other hand, Form 6 applications were filed by first-time voters as well as people whose names had been deleted from the draft rolls after being categorised as Absent, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate or Others (ASDDO).
To verify the additions, The Hindu compared the final electoral rolls with Form 9 reports, which consolidate details of Form 6 applications, and Form 11A and 11B reports, which contain records of Form 8 applications for shifting voters within and outside an Assembly constituency, respectively. The analysis found that 1,13,059 additions could not be matched to either set of records.
Across the city
This pattern was seen across the city. In 25 of Bengaluru’s 28 Assembly constituencies, at least 35% of the new enrolments could not be traced to Form 6 or Form 8 records.
Bangalore South Assembly constituency had the highest number of untraceable new enrolments. Of the 20,914 new enrolments in its final roll, 9,434 (45.1%) could not be traced to either Form 6 or Form 8 records.
Mahadevapura (9,279), K.R. Pura (8,013), Yeshwanthapura (7,373) and Byatarayanapura (6,885) also recorded high numbers of untraceable additions. Together with Bangalore South, these five constituencies accounted for 40,984 names, or 36.3% of the 1,13,059 additions across Bengaluru that could not be traced to Form 6 or Form 8 records.
The Chief Electoral Officer’s office said it had all the Form 6 applications and that many may not be reflected in the Form 9 reports because they had been filed outside the claims and objections period (August 24 to September 23). It said Form 9 reports were made available only during this period.
However, the CEO’s website continues to host the consolidated Form 9 reports even after the period ended.
Published - November 17, 2026 06:00 am IST

stories.headline: Wheels of justice grind slowly
stories.deck: Bengaluru's lower courts are currently grappling with a staggering backlog of over 430,000 pending cases. The influx of new filings is surpassing the rate of case disposals, exacerbating the already high pendency rates. Particularly, the Chief Judicial Magistrate court has reported a sharp rise in criminal case pending this year.
stories.bodyText:
More than 4.3 lakh cases were pending before the city’s lower courts – which handle burglary, cheating, domestic violence, cheque-bounce, rash driving, rioting, and rent disputes, among other cases – as of Sept 2026. The justice-delivery system is sizable, spread over roughly 80 magistrate halls, about 20 small causes halls, and over 120 civil halls, including commercial courts. Even so, fresh filings continue to outpace disposals, and pendency is rising in most units.
CJM COURT UNIT
This is the biggest pressure point, with 2.4 lakh criminal cases pending this year, up from 1.6 lakh in 2023. The Chief Judicial Magistrate court unit hears theft, burglary, cheating, forgery, criminal breach of trust, assault, grievous hurt and domestic violence complaints. It also routinely handles cheque-bounce disputes under the Negotiable Instruments Act, major rash-driving accident cases, public nuisance and rioting.
COURT OF SMALL CAUSES
Of 95,816 cases (23,257 civil and 72,559 criminal), 95,446 were pending (22,957 civil and 72,489 criminal). Pendency stood at 95,808 in 2024, so the backlog has barely moved. The court hears straightforward money-recovery and rent disputes with claims up to Rs 2 lakh where ownership isn't contested.
CITY CIVIL COURT AND MAYO HALL UNIT
In these two courts, of 57,679 civil and 30,844 criminal cases, 57,472 and 31,182 cases were pending, respectively. These hear disputes between individuals over property and personal rights, including injunction, declaration and partition suits, as well as neighbourhood quarrels such as damage from adjacent construction.
COMMERCIAL COURTS
Of 5,157 civil and four criminal cases in such courts, 5,053 and three were pending, respectively. These courts deal purely with financial matters between companies, such as a bank suing a firm over a loan. Under Commercial Courts Act, parties must first approach the District Legal Services Authority, which has a unit at the City Civil Court complex and offers pre-litigation settlement. Rent and eviction disputes over commercial premises such as hotels or offices fall exclusively under these courts.
NAME-CHANGE MATTERS
Name-change matters also land here. Experts said corrections to names and identity details in certificates are largely handled administratively, through a notarised affidavit, a newspaper publication and a govt gazette notification. A declaration suit becomes necessary only if the issuing authority formally rejects the application. TOI observed that a large share of the cases concerned name changes in school or birth certificates. Administrative adjustments and case movements between court halls often see the closing balance become higher than the opening one.
WHAT SYSTEM NEEDS
Senior advocates attribute pendency to interim applications, staff shortage, rising family cases and the absence of fast-track courts. The system needs more judges, staff and funds. Gurupasrad MN, senior advocate, said: “Fresh cases come in every day and interim applications keep stalling the main trial. Unless the interim part is settled, the main case cannot move.”
AP Ranganatha, former president, Advocates Association of Bengaluru, said: “Courts need more judges, staff and separate funds. Every new law brings a special court without the facilities to run it.”

stories.headline: Bengaluru's historic Kumara Krupa guest house, where Mahatma Gandhi once stayed, becomes DK Shivakumar's new home office, named 'Ganga'
stories.deck: Chief Minister DK Shivakumar will officially move into the newly named heritage bungalow Ganga shortly. The previous residence, Kumara Krupa guest house, was renovated and had its rooms named after Karnataka rivers. Shivakumar plans to host all 224 MLAs, MPs, and MLCs in this new location soon. The opposition has criticized this move, claiming it disrespects the building's historical significance.
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Come Thursday, chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
 will have a new address for his home office here, with a new name, too: Ganga.
The 160-year-old heritage bungalow, until now known as Kumara Krupa guest house, has been renovated and rechristened, with its rooms and meeting spaces also named after Karnataka rivers.
The CM's first choice, Cauvery, on Kumara Krupa Road, remains occupied as his predecessor Siddaramaiah is yet to move out. It had housed several CMs earlier, including Shivakumar's mentor SM Krishna.
Anugraha next door was abandoned decades ago over Vaastu concerns, while Shivakumar did not prefer the British-era Race Course Road bungalow that former CMs BS Yediyurappa and Basavaraj Bommai called home. So, the choice narrowed down to Ganga.
The CM said he will invite all 224 MLAs, MPs and MLCs to ‘Ganga’ on Thursday, when he will begin meeting people there.
Kota stone flooring at Rs 60 per unit and marble or granite at about Rs 80 per unit were used to refurbish the structure.
The decision to move the CM’s official residence to Ganga had drawn flak from the opposition even before Shivakumar could make his choice public, with BJP and JD(S) accusing him of misusing a heritage property belonging to govt and altering a structure built in 1856.
“Converting heritage building Kumara Krupa, associated with the memories of Deewan K Seshadri Iyer and where the Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi, had once stayed, into the CM’s home office, merely to satisfy personal desires, is a great betrayal of history,” they had alleged.
However, defending the move, Shivakumar reasoned: Since the facility should not go to waste, I have taken this decision.” Moreover, only about 10% of the building was modified, retaining its heritage identity, he added.
The expenses, the chief minister said, were mainly for security, including work on the compound.

stories.headline: 29th edition of Bengaluru Tech Summit to kick off on November 17
stories.deck: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar will inaugurate the three-day event, themed: “AI & Beyond,” on Tuesday morning
stories.bodyText:
Karnataka is set to host the 29th edition of its flagship annual technology exposition, the Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS), from November 17 to 19 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC).
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar will inaugurate the three-day event, themed: “AI & Beyond,” on Tuesday morning.
Addressing a media conference on the eve of the summit, Minister for Home, IT & BT, and e-Governance Priyank Kharge said that the conference would feature over 120 knowledge sessions across 16 thematic tracks, including IT & DeepTech, Frontier Tech, Electro-Semicon, Electric Mobility, Health & Biotech, Digital Infrastructure & Data Centres, Data & Cybersecurity, Assistive Tech, Focus GCC, Circular Economy, Orange Economy, Finverse, Skilling & Edutech, India–USA Tech Conclave, Global Collaborations, and India Innovates.
Highlighting the summit’s global trajectory, Mr. Kharge noted how the expo has expanded over the decades to draw international participation. “Bengaluru Tech Summit has evolved beyond an annual technology gathering into a platform where global conversations translate into partnerships, investments, and tangible opportunities,” the Minister said.
The State’s ambition was to make Bengaluru a gateway for the world to engage with India’s technology ecosystem, while taking Karnataka’s innovations and solutions to global markets, he added.
According to Mr. Kharge, the 2026 edition introduces several new initiatives, including the debut of the GCC India Leaders’ Dialogue on Wednesday and a new Workshops & Masterclass Series featuring 11 sessions by global firms such as Nvidia, Cloudflare, and eBay. The summit will also host three co-located international events: the maiden edition of Germany’s embedded world India, alongside France-origin sustainability and health forums ChangeNOW and One Sustainable Health.
A 50,000 sq. ft. AI & Robotics Pavilion co-curated by Bharat1.ai, showcasing indigenous humanoids, drones, and India’s first quadrupedal athletic showcase, would be a new feature. The summit will also mark the launch of AI Kavach, the country’s first AI cybersecurity lab for the BFSI (banking, financial services and insurance) sector developed with IIT Kanpur.
Backed by Karnataka’s Global Innovation Alliance, which has expanded from 10 countries in 2018 to over 40 nations, the event will have Sweden as its Country Partner, alongside delegations from over 65 countries. Over 1,000 startups from 100 Indian cities will participate, culminating on November 19 with the Future Makers Conclave to celebrate 10 years of Karnataka’s ELEVATE initiative and felicitate recent unicorns and IPO achievers.
Published - November 16, 2026 11:55 pm IST

stories.headline: Karnataka to ban half-helmets, mandate meters for app-based taxis: Minister
stories.bodyText:
Karnataka Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh said Monday that the government was in the process of banning half-helmets for two-wheeler riders and that the ban would be enforced by the end of this year.
A half-helmet covers only the top of the head while leaving the face, chin, ears, and lower neck exposed. Though relatively cheaper than a full-face helmet, it doesn’t offer adequate protection.
Suresh earlier said the government would target both sellers and manufacturers of half-helmets. In October, the transport department and home department submitted a proposal to the government seeking legal opinion on banning half-helmets.
Meters mandatory for app-based taxis too
Addressing a press conference in Bengaluru, the minister also said that all taxis, including those of Ola and Uber, would have to install meters. Taxi companies must charge passengers only the fare fixed by the government, he said, adding that violators would be punished.
Suresh also said the framework and rules for making meters mandatory were being prepared and that the law would be enforced soon. He said the aim is to protect vehicle owners and drivers from exploitation by app-based taxi companies. He added that taxi owners and drivers had asked the government to mandate meters, alleging exploitation by app-based companies.
Fines for riding two-wheelers on footpaths have been doubled, Suresh said. A first offence will attract a fine of Rs 5,000 and a second offence Rs 10,000. For a third offence, the vehicle will be seized. He said rules for this are also being framed and will be enforced after government approval.
No more Green SM taxis for now
Suresh said 100 taxis of Green SM, a Vietnam-based taxi company, have already been registered. The transport department has now been strictly instructed not to register any new Green SM taxis until further orders, he said. Responding to a question, he said whether to grant the company further permission would be decided after discussing the matter with the chief minister.
Suresh said the government would act to protect the interests of the state’s drivers. He further said the government had released Rs 280 crore towards wage arrears in the four state-owned road transport corporations. The remaining Rs 300 crore will be released soon, subject to availability of funds, he said.

briefs.headline: EC orders SSR in Karnataka, ‘left out’ voters in focus
briefs.deck: The Election Commission of India will begin a special summary revision in Karnataka starting December 1. This process aims to enroll eligible voters who were previously excluded from the electoral rolls. The integrated draft electoral rolls will be published, and claims can be submitted until December 31. Final electoral rolls are scheduled to be released on January 20, 2027.
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Weeks after SIR removed more than 99 lakh voters from Karnataka’s final electoral rolls, EC has ordered a special summary revision (SSR) in the state to enrol eligible voters who were “left out” and first-time electors, reports Pearl DSouza.
According to the schedule issued by EC Monday, the public phase of the process begins on Dec 1, with publication of the integrated draft electoral rolls. Claims can be filed till Dec 31. Final rolls will be out on Jan 20.
EC has laid down safeguards for deletions. EROs must personally verify cases where deletions exceed 2% of electors in a polling station, or where one person has filed objections in more than five cases.
In case of every deletion, the EROs must pass a reasoned order, allow the affected person a hearing, and upload the order on ECINET. Officials deployed for SSR cannot be transferred from Dec 1 to Jan 20, 2027 (final rolls) without EC’s permission.

briefs.headline: 100-cab cap for Green SM; digital meters to be a must for all cabs in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: The Karnataka transport department has decided to stop further registration of electric taxis from Green SM. This decision aims to protect local taxi drivers worried about livelihoods being affected. Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh has indicated that the company will be limited to operating just 100 taxis. Drivers have expressed concerns over low fare rates impacting their income and financial…
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Following pressure from taxi drivers’ unions, the Karnataka transport department has decided against allowing further registration of e-taxis operated by Vietnam-based electric mobility firm Green SM.
Transport minister Byrathi Suresh said the company had already been granted permission to operate 100 taxis in Bengaluru. The company will be allowed to launch operations with these vehicles. However, instructions had been issued to Regional Transport Office (RTO) officials not to register any additional taxis by the company, he said.
Suresh said the decision was aimed at protecting the livelihoods of taxi drivers in the state.
“We have received information that they are planning to register 10,000 electric taxis and charge Rs 8 to Rs 10 per km. This will affect the livelihoods of people. I will discuss the issue with the chief minister. Representatives of the company had met me seeking permission. I have said no to them,” he said.
Taxi drivers’ unions have been opposing Green SM, arguing that its company-owned fleet could threaten the livelihoods of independent drivers who have invested their savings or taken loans to purchase vehicles.
They fear that the large-scale induction of electric taxis, coupled with app-based operations, could give the company an unfair competitive advantage and trigger a price war. Drivers also argue that fares as low as Rs 8 per km would make it difficult for individual operators to meet their equated monthly instalments (EMIs) and operating expenses.
Taxi and autorickshaw associations claim that nearly eight lakh families in Bengaluru depend on the sector for their livelihood. They have demanded that the government impose a cap on Green SM’s fleet.
Digital meters a must, No app-based fare collection
The govt will make installation of digital meters mandatory for all taxis, including those operating through app-based aggregators such as Ola and Uber, the minister said. Taxi operators will be allowed to collect only fares fixed by the govt. Vehicles found violating the rules will be seized. He said fares must be collected through digital meters and not through app-based fare calculations.
The transport department is drafting legal framework to enforce the requirement. Suresh said taxi owners and drivers had approached the govt seeking mandatory installation of meters, alleging that app-based companies were exploiting them through arbitrary fare collection.
However, this is not the first time thegovt has proposed mandatory installation of digital meters in taxis. Similar attempts were made in the past, but officials themselves are yet to have clarity on the specifications of the meters, who would bear the installation cost, the price of the devices and other technical requirements. The proposed rules will also apply to independent taxi operators. Suresh said vehicles that do not have digital meters installed will be seized.
Ban on half-helmets by New Year
There will be a ban on the use of half-helmets across the state to improve the safety of two-wheeler riders and pillion riders.
The minister said a decision had already been taken and the rules required to implement the ban were being framed. The govt aims to enforce the new regulations by the end of this year.
The penalties for riding two-wheelers on footpaths had been increased to Rs 5,000 for the first offence and Rs 10,000 for the second. Vehicles will be seized if riders are caught committing the offence for a third time, subject to the proposed legal provisions and govt approval.
Rs 280 cr released for RTC employees’ wage arrears
Govt has released Rs 280 crore towards pending wage arrears of employees of the state’s four transport corporations.
Suresh said a total of Rs 1,200 crore was due in wage arrears, of which Rs 450 crore had been released in the first instalment and Rs 170 crore in the second.
With the latest release of Rs 280 crore, the total amount disbursed so far has reached Rs 900 crore. He said steps had been taken to release the remaining Rs 300 crore in phases, subject to the availability of funds.
BOX
40 staff issued notices for fake diplomas
Responding to allegations that some in-service employees had submitted fake certificates to secure promotions as motor vehicle inspectors, the minister said show-cause notices had been issued to 40 employees.
“As per the information I have received, 10 employees have submitted genuine certificates, while the remaining have not. Only those with genuine certificates will be considered for the selection process,” he said.

briefs.headline: Software glitch halts trade licence issuance across Bengaluru for three months
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Trade licence issuance has been stalled across five city corporations for nearly three months due to technical issues with the new software being introduced by Greater Bengaluru Authority. The transition from the old system to the new one has disrupted both fresh applications and licence renewals. Result: business establishments are unable to obtain necessary permissions.
A commissioner of one of the five city corporations confirmed to 
TOI that the service has been disrupted as the new software is yet to be activated. “The old system is also unavailable. Licences are not being issued manually in the meantime either,” he said, adding the disruption has resulted in significant revenue loss for the corporations.
A senior GBA official said the authority is transitioning to a new platform after facing several problems with the old software and following directions from high court to introduce a more effective system. “Login credentials are being provided to the vendor to integrate the system. This process should be completed in about a week, after which the service is expected to resume,” the official said.
The expansion from 198 wards under erstwhile BBMP to 369 wards under GBA had added to the complexity of the rollout. 
The new software is being developed by a Delhi-based firm, and coordination between the agencies has also contributed to delays, the official added.
A health officer said the new system is being developed in accordance with court directions and will incorporate additional checks and documentation. These include road width, road history, approved building plans, property tax-paid receipts, khata and occupancy certificates. It will also classify establishments into food and non-food commercial categories.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru leads country in voluntary disclosure of foreign assets
briefs.deck: FAST-DS 2026, which offers small taxpayers a faceless opportunity to disclose previously undeclared foreign assets or foreign-sourced income, will expire on December 31, 2026
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru has emerged as the leading centre in the country for voluntary foreign asset disclosures under the Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers-Disclosure Scheme (FAST-DS) 2026, accounting for 217 applications out of 1,026 Form 1 submissions received across various Principal Chief Commissioner of Income Tax jurisdictions as of October 20.
Disclosing the figures at an outreach programme organised by the Bangalore Chamber of Industry and Commerce (BCIC) here on Monday, Manjit Singh, Chief Commissioner of Income Tax (TDS), Bengaluru, said the city’s response was significantly ahead of other jurisdictions, reflecting growing awareness among taxpayers about foreign asset reporting requirements.
The outreach programme focused on creating awareness about FAST-DS 2026, which provides eligible small taxpayers with a one-time, faceless opportunity to disclose previously undeclared foreign assets or foreign-sourced income within prescribed thresholds and obtain relief from penal and prosecution consequences under the Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) and Imposition of Tax Act, 2015, subject to the scheme’s conditions. The scheme, which opened on August 16, 2026, will remain available until December 31, 2026.
While delivering the keynote address, Mr. Singh said, “Bengaluru is the highest with 217 forms, while others are far away. The Income Tax Department had undertaken extensive outreach initiatives, including engagement with approximately 267 companies whose employees could potentially benefit from the scheme.”
Online awareness programmes have also been conducted to explain the disclosure requirements and encourage eligible taxpayers to come forward, he noted. Mr. Singh also observed that overseas travel and foreign financial exposure have become increasingly common among professionals and businessmen. Inadvertent omissions in reporting foreign assets could expose taxpayers to penalties or notices at a later stage, making timely voluntary disclosure particularly important.
“As Indian businesses and professionals become increasingly integrated with the global economy through overseas investments, ESOPs, foreign bank accounts, and cross-border transactions, international tax reporting has become both essential and complex,” commented K. Ravi, President, BCIC.
Many small taxpayers and returning professionals inadvertently overlook reporting overseas holdings, often without any intention of evading taxes; however, FAST-DS 2026 provided a timely opportunity to regularise such omissions, he pointed out.
I-T dept seeks inputs
According to Mr. Singh, the Income Tax Department has been seeking industry inputs on digital economy taxation. The tax administration must evolve with emerging digital platforms, content creators, and new business models, he said, adding that a committee has been constituted in his office to engage with stakeholders and seek suggestions on simplifying tax compliance.

briefs.headline: Karnataka to prohibit use of half helmets by New Year
briefs.bodyText:
Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh on Monday announced that the government was in the process of framing a law to prohibit the use of half helmets across Karnataka. The rule is expected to come into force by the New Year.
At a recent inter-departmental meeting attended by officials of the Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP) and the Transport Department, several issues, including traffic congestion and road safety, were discussed. During the meeting, officials proposed making full helmets mandatory even for pillion riders, pointing out that the primary purpose of wearing a helmet was safety, which half helmets failed to ensure.
The Transport Department examined the legal provisions for implementing the rule and has now moved forward with the proposal.
According to BTP data, riding without a helmet and pillion riding without a helmet continue to be the two categories under which the highest number of cases are registered every year.

briefs.headline: After SIR deletions, Karnataka plans police-led household survey in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
The Karnataka government is set to conduct a door-to-door data collection exercise throughout Bengaluru to create household-level records of residents through the police department, Chief Minister D K Shivakumar announced Sunday. This initiative comes after the release of the final Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls on October 27, which deleted over 43 lakh voters in Bengaluru.
After inaugurating a community hall, a modern techno-gym, and a badminton court during the ‘Bharathinagar Habba’ festival in Bengaluru, CM Shivakumar said, “To ensure residents’ safety, there is a pressing need to collect household-level data across the city. It has also come to our notice that Bengaluru’s electoral roll has shrunk from 51 lakh to 45 lakh voters. Given this, instructions will be issued to ensure the police department maintains accurate records of who resides where in the city.”
A home department official said, “We have not yet discussed how this will be implemented. Given that we have a beat system in place, local police officers and wardens will be assigned to collect the data. However, this will be a significant task to undertake.”
Schemes for street vendors, traffic management
Shivakumar said the government has rolled out several schemes to support the unemployed and is taking steps to rehabilitate street vendors, with roughly 30,000 vendors already identified.
“In the first phase, tenders have been floated to provide vending vehicles to 1,500 beneficiaries. Additionally, the Social Welfare Department is implementing various projects worth Rs 352 crore to benefit around 15,000 to 17,000 people,” he said.
“Maintaining law and order in Bengaluru is a top priority. Special measures are underway to crack down on crime, rowdyism, and the drug menace. Our goal is to foster an environment where citizens can walk the streets safely and with dignity even at midnight or 2 am. To achieve this, the Home Department has been directed to set up a dedicated wing,” he said.
Addressing Bengaluru’s traffic woes, Shivakumar said, “With the number of vehicles in Bengaluru touching 1.40 crore, traffic congestion has become a massive challenge. Narrow roads, surging vehicle numbers, and legal hurdles in property acquisition make road widening difficult. If a single building demolition case lands in court, it can drag on for years. Therefore, the government is exploring practical alternatives to resolve the city’s infrastructure bottlenecks.”

briefs.headline: Former friend allegedly put Rs 30-lakh price on Bengaluru realtor’s life
briefs.bodyText:
A former friend allegedly orchestrated the killing of a Bengaluru realtor last week following a financial dispute that had ended their association two years ago, with the police saying on Monday the murder was executed for Rs 30 lakh.
G K Mithin, Deputy Commissioner of Police, Northeast Division, said they have arrested five people, including a former associate, Kiran, who executed the murder of realtor Charan Gowda alias Charan M N, 40, through two hired killers identified as Kiran and Akash.
Apart from Kiran and the killers, two of his friends and an intermediary have also been arrested.
Friend-turned-foe
The police said Gowda and Kiran were friends and associates before they fell out around two years ago over financial transactions.
They said Kiran told two of his friends, Roopesh and Rudresh, about the dispute and sought their help. Roopesh arranged the murder through an intermediary identified as Lokesh, the police said.
Gowda, who operated a real estate firm called Dhani Properties, was murdered in front of his wife last Friday outside his office in Yelahanka New Town. He was hacked to death soon after he parked his car and got out to go up to his first-floor office.
His wife, Vimarshini, 37, an information technology engineer and a partner in several businesses, filed a complaint with the Yelahanka New Town police on November 13, stating that two unidentified men wielding machetes hacked her husband to death in front of her when they arrived at the office.
Gowda, a native of Channapatna and father of a 10-year-old child, had been in the real estate business for around 10 years.
The victim and his wife ran multiple businesses before entering real estate. They had a company called All Dimension in 2016, which sold fridge magnets, key chains, gift boxes, and other miscellaneous items.
The couple also had a real estate venture called Dream Plot Factory LLP and recently started a film production studio.

briefs.headline: ‘Mom can’t talk on bus’: Bengaluru killer tricked 11-year-old to hide parents’ deaths
briefs.bodyText:
An 11-year-old boy who survived an alleged mass murder spree in Bengaluru by his cab driver uncle was misled about the whereabouts of his parents by his teenage cousin, a suspected accomplice to the killings, according to police investigations.
The boy has emerged as a key witness in the murders of seven members of a family in north Bengaluru allegedly by cab driver S Indushekhar, 52, with the assistance of his 17-year-old daughter between October 16 and October 31. The final victims on October 31 were Shankar, 44, the cab driver’s brother-in-law, and his wife Nalini, 29, who were the boy’s parents.
Police investigations found that the killer and his daughter allegedly hid the murders of the boy’s parents from him even as they took him along in Indushekhar’s cab to dispose of their bodies in the Shiradi Ghat region. Found in the company of the teenage girl on November 3, following the cab driver’s arrest, the boy felt secure with his cousin sister and acted on her instructions without any coercion or force when talking to relatives after his parents went missing on October 31, police sources said.
The probe indicates that the boy was led to believe his parents were travelling separately on a bus for a long religious family tour while he travelled with his uncle and cousin. “The boy was replying at the instance of his cousin. He trusted her and was unaware of what had happened. He acted on the promptings of his cousin and her father,” a police source said.
The police also suspect that Indushekhar had planned to kill the 11-year-old boy as well, but may have dropped the plan after phone calls from relatives indicated that the police were likely to be alerted to trace the missing parents.
Phone recordings with grandmother
The police have recovered voice recordings of phone conversations between the mobile phones of the boy’s mother and his grandmother following the October 31 murders. In the recordings, the worried grandmother is heard imploring the boy to let her speak to his mother, while the boy insists his parents are inside a bus on a religious trip and unable to talk.
“Please give the phone to your mother just once, darling,” the grandmother is heard saying, to which the boy replies, “They are not allowing it.” She pleads further. “Give it to her, dear. I will stay on the line; go give it to her for just one second, son. Everyone is scared; we need to hear her voice, dear. Please go.”
In another recording, the grandmother expresses fear and mentions filing a police complaint since the couple had been missing for three days. When asked why he was not attending school, the boy claimed his mother had informed the school about the family trip, adding, “Mom won’t even take the phone to talk right now. They won’t give it to her while on the bus.”
Property dispute motive
The killing spree began on October 16, with the murders of Indushekhar’s wife Sunitha M J, 40; and her mother Rupavathi, 65. He then allegedly lured his wife’s other relatives to his house separately, serving them drinks laced with tablets that left them unconscious before killing them.
The victims included his wife’s first brother Shivakumar, 46; his wife Divya, 30; and their son Puneeth, 7, followed by second brother-in-law Shankar, 44; and his wife Nalini, 29. The police said Indushekhar convinced his college-going daughter to become an associate by holding out the prospect of gaining property, and she assisted by washing the crime scene at their home and cleaning up evidence.
The police said Indushekhar orchestrated the murders after a falling out with his wife in a bid to acquire a Bengaluru property worth nearly Rs 3 crore belonging to Rupavathi, which was intended to be transferred to her sons.
Seemanth Kumar Singh, Police Commissioner, said last week that a financial angle had emerged alongside personal motives and was being examined. Following Indushekhar’s detention, the police recovered the first body, that of his seven-year-old nephew, in the Nandi Hills region on November 5. The bodies of his wife and mother-in-law were later found in the Yercaud hill region near Salem in Tamil Nadu; those of Shivakumar and Divya at Chamundi Hills near Mysuru; and those of the 11-year-old survivor’s parents at Shiradi Ghats near Mangaluru.

stories.headline: What’s behind the record ₹89,856-crore FPI surge into Indian equities? | Explained
stories.deck: The recent slowdown in AI stocks and concerns about their growth prospects have brought investors seeking a safer bet back to India
stories.bodyText:
The story so far: Amid escalating geopolitical tensions, a boom in the AI sector, and valuation concerns, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have been exiting the Indian market for the last two years. However, in a change of course, FPIs have returned to India, and pumped the Indian markets with all-time high inflows of ₹89,856 crore so far in November.
The recent slowdown in AI stocks and concerns about their growth prospects have brought investors seeking a safer bet back to India. The boom in global AI and tech stocks over the last two years prompted investors to move too heavily into tech-heavy countries like the U.S., South Korea, and Taiwan.

stories.deck: The 30-share BSE Sensex advanced 108.83 points to 82,184.33 in early trade. The 50-share NSE Nifty rose 31.90 points to 25,325.75
stories.bodyText:

From the Sensex pack, InterGlobe Aviation, Maruti Suzuki, Adani Ports, Mahindra & Mahindra, Axis Bank and State Bank of India were among the major winners.
Tech Mahindra, HCL Tech, Power Grid and NTPC were among the laggards.
Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, traded 0.88% lower at $91.65 per barrel.
Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) bought equities worth ₹4,864.68 crore on Monday (November 16), according to exchange data.

This complete dramatic reversal of the FPI flows, aided by impressive earnings growth as reflected in the Q2 results, will impart resilience to the Indian market despite the turmoil in global markets," said V.K. Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments Ltd.
The continuing winding down of AI trade in the U.S. (Nasdaq down by 2.49%) is impacting markets such as South Korea, Taiwan and Japan, he said.
"This, again, is a blessing in disguise for India," Mr. Vijayakumar added.

The U.S. equity markets ended lower on Monday (November 16). The Nasdaq Composite tanked 2.49%, the S&P 500 was down 1.92%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 1.41%.

stories.headline: Trump’s Nvidia stake grew to as much as $62 million: Report
stories.deck: Donald Trump's stake in Nvidia has escalated significantly, potentially reaching up to $62 million recently. Frequent trading of Nvidia shares by Trump's investment accounts has raised concerns over potential conflicts of interest. The scrutiny comes following the resignation of Jensen Huang, who had a controversial personal life involving alleged espionage ties. Nvidia's business dealings with…
stories.bodyText:
US President Donald Trump has stood by Nvidia’s former boss Jensen Huang despite a string of personal scandals, including an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
But there is another Nvidia connection drawing attention: Trump's own stock portfolio.
His investments in the AI chipmaker have grown sharply over the past year, with financial disclosures suggesting that his stake could be worth as much as $62 million.
The disclosures put Trump's Nvidia holdings under the spotlight as the company grapples with controversy surrounding Huang's resignation and its business dealings with China.
Trump's Nvidia stake
Trump’s Nvidia holdings, estimated at between $615,000 and $1.3 million at the end of 2024, rose to as much as $62 million within the last year, according to financial disclosures reviewed by The Washington Post. However, these filings do not include trades made over the past two months, so the latest value of his holdings could be even higher, The Independent reported.
But the value of his holdings is only part of the picture. Since returning to the White House, Trump's investment accounts have been actively buying and selling Nvidia shares.
A CNBC analysis of his annual and periodic financial disclosures found that his accounts had bought or sold Nvidia shares at least 103 times. 
The transactions were worth a combined $27 million to $97.5 million.
The exact size of Trump's current stake, however, remains unclear. His disclosures report investments in broad dollar-value ranges rather than the actual number of shares held. Based on the holdings reported in August, his Nvidia investment would have been worth between $4.5 million and $57.7 million by midday Monday, when the stock was trading at around $157.
The latest disclosures do not capture transactions from the past two months, making it difficult to establish how much Nvidia stock Trump currently owns.
Trump's investment accounts sold between $500,001 and $1 million worth of Nvidia shares on May 18, the first Monday after his return from a China visit with Huang. The sale was part of a wider trading spree, with Trump disclosing more than 21,000 trades in 2025, compared with roughly 500 during his entire first term, according to CNBC's analysis.
White House response to questions over Trump's Nvidia holdings
The scale of Trump's Nvidia investments has also raised questions about his financial interests in the company, particularly given his close relationship with Huang and his administration's decisions on export controls.
The administration has opened the door for Nvidia to do business in China, while Trump has repeatedly defended its approach to export restrictions against criticism. These decisions have come under scrutiny as the company faces questions over its China-related business and the allegations surrounding Huang.
White House officials have repeatedly maintained that Trump does not personally select or trade individual stocks. The president has also rejected calls to sell his stock holdings.
According to the White House, Trump's assets are held in a trust managed by his children, while independent financial managers handle his investment portfolio.
‘She may not be a spy,’ says Trump
Trump has also appeared to question his administration's assessment of Alice Huang's alleged links to Chinese intelligence.
“I don’t know that she’s a spy at all. Nobody's proven that,” he told reporters outside the White House on Monday. “He probably shouldn’t have been doing, on a personal basis, what he did. You know, from — who knows? That's a different story. But nobody's proven that she's a spy. She may not be a spy,” he said.
Nvidia shares were trading at around $157.72 on Monday, down more than 3.1% during the day. The decline came as investors reacted to Huang's resignation ahead of the company's third-quarter earnings call scheduled for Tuesday.
Huang stepped down last Thursday following revelations about his relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer, who is suspected of being a spy.

stories.headline: India faces 'acute' aircraft shortage, needs more than 1,000 planes: Piyush Goyal
stories.deck: In an effort to address soaring air traffic demands, India plans to procure an extra 1,000 civilian aircraft. The government has underscored the importance of expedited delivery from credible manufacturers to increase the fleet size. This expansion is set to enhance air connectivity with Egypt, paving the way for new flight options.
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India is looking to add another 1,000 civilian aircraft to its existing orders as it struggles to keep up with rising air traffic demand amid an "acute" shortage of planes, Union minister 
Piyush Goyal
 said.
The government is also pushing established aircraft manufacturers to speed up supplies.
Speaking to reporters during his two-day visit to Egypt, Goyal said expanding the aircraft fleet would help improve air connectivity between the two countries and create room for more flights.
"We need to see more (air) connectivity... as we get more aircraft, we are sure we will be able to have more flights to Egypt," he said.
Goyal is in Egypt to explore opportunities to strengthen trade and investment ties between the two countries. Currently, EgyptAir operates direct flights connecting India and Egypt.
Pointing to the scale of India's aircraft requirements, the minister said the country had already ordered more than 1,200 planes but would need over 2,000 aircraft to meet its requirements. It is now prepared to place orders for another 1,000 planes, while pressing manufacturers to ensure quicker deliveries.
"We have ordered more than 1,200 planes, and we are ready to order another 1,000 planes; we need more than 2,000 planes for our requirements. 
So we are pursuing the established manufacturers of aircraft for faster supplies," Goyal said.
He reiterated that the arrival of more aircraft would allow Indian airlines to operate additional flights to Egypt.
India is one of the world's fastest-growing civil aviation markets, with airlines IndiGo and Air India having placed substantial aircraft orders with Airbus and Boeing for deliveries in the coming years.
The country is also seeing the presence of several major international aerospace companies. Airbus has two final assembly lines in India, catering to military transport aircraft and helicopters.
Global aircraft manufacturers Boeing and Airbus also source components and services worth around $2 billion every year from India. Meanwhile, Brazilian aircraft maker Embraer has partnered with the Adani Group under a strategic collaboration to explore setting up regional aircraft manufacturing in India.

stories.headline: At Finance Ministry’s 1st pre-Budget meet, economists debate LTCG tax
stories.bodyText:
As the government began its pre-Budget consultations on Monday, the issue of Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax on equities was a keenly debated subject at a meeting of economists with officials from the Ministry of Finance.
The meeting, chaired by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, saw certain economists suggest that the LTCG tax on equities need not be reduced and concessions should not be made to foreign investors. At the same time, opposing views were also made.
“It was debated a lot, but no consensus emerged,” a person aware of the discussions said. Another person who participated in the meeting said granular inputs came from all those in attendance and there was no one dominant view.
However, others said there were “not many takers” for cutting the LTCG tax now that circumstances have changed, with foreign inflows into India seeing a sharp turnaround in recent weeks.
The first half of November has seen Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) buy $9.53 billion worth of Indian shares — the highest monthly purchase on record — marking a remarkable turnaround that has helped propel the Nifty 14% higher over the last five weeks.
“The government officials did not say anything and heard the economists out. But the mood in the room was not in favour of cutting or giving concessions on LTCG tax to foreign investors,” another participant told The Indian Express.
Calls for tax relief
Ever since the Centre and the Reserve Bank of India took measures in June to support the rupee and encourage inflows by removing capital gains and withholding taxes on foreigners’ investments into government bonds, there have been calls from foreign investors, tax experts, and industry leaders that India should either remove or lower the LTCG tax on equities. This currently stands at 12.5%.
Deliberations have also been held within the government on whether this relief should be provided. Speaking at an event last month, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman had said the debate on LTCG tax is “healthy” and she is “keen” to hear about it.
The Indian Express reported last month that the government’s internal deliberations in the run-up to next year’s Budget include lowering LTCG tax for both domestic and foreign investors and letting foreign investors pay this tax on the gains made in dollar terms as opposed to in rupee terms.
So far in 2026-27 as a whole, FPIs remain net sellers of Indian shares to the tune of $7.67 billion. In 2024-25 and 2025-26 combined, FPIs’ net sales of domestic stocks were $34.32 billion.
“The global economic scenario is going to change and more stability is now expected in light of the US midterm election results. The Indian economy is in a good condition,” the person cited above said.
Fiscal prudence stressed
The government’s finances were another key theme that was discussed at the meeting on Monday, with multiple participants saying everyone felt fiscal prudence should continue. Continued focus on public investments was also emphasised, they said.
The Union Budget for 2026-27 targeted a fiscal deficit of 4.3% of GDP. However, soon after the Budget was presented, the war in West Asia began, leading to a surge in global commodity prices, including those of energy and fertilisers — two of India’s key imports.
On inflation, economists were of the view that the current high prints were not very disturbing, considering they are not expected to remain elevated on a sustained basis. Data released last week showed India’s headline retail inflation crossed 6% for the first time in two years in October.
Other senior finance ministry officials were also part of the meeting, including Economic Affairs Secretary Anuradha Thakur and Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran. Later in the day, Sitharaman chaired a second pre-Budget consultation meeting with experts from agriculture and rural development sectors.

briefs.headline: A poverty line that falls short
briefs.deck: Reliable poverty estimates are not just for academic purposes. India has made real progress, but without a credible benchmark, it is hard to say how much, or how much remains to be done
briefs.bodyText:
There is no serious doubt that poverty in India has fallen sharply over the past decade. However, researchers and policymakers cannot agree on how many are still poor. Depending on the estimate, the share ranges from about 5% to more than 26%. Take the recent World Bank report. At its international line of $3 a day (2021 PPP), 2.6% of Indians were poor in 2022-23. Raise the line to $4.20, the bank’s benchmark for lower middle-income countries, and the figure jumps to around 16.1%. Same country, same year. Only the yardstick changed. A low level of extreme poverty does not necessarily mean poverty is not still a major issue. Where you draw the line decides how much economic insecurity you see.
India’s own figures tell a similar convoluted story. For example, SBI Research (2025) takes the Tendulkar line of 2009, adjusts it for inflation, and gets poverty of 7.2% in rural India and 4.6% in urban India for 2022-23. Rangarajan and Dev (2014), using an inflation-adjusted version of the Rangarajan Committee line, arrive at 10.8%. Further, Sethu, Surya and Ruthu (2024), who rebuild the Rangarajan method from the latest consumption survey, report 26.4%. Most of that gap boils down to the lines themselves: SBI’s Tendulkar-based lines use, after adjusting for inflation, about ₹1,632 a month per person in rural areas and ₹1,944 in urban areas. In contrast, Sethu et al. use much higher thresholds of ₹2,515 and ₹3,639. And the outcomes are obvious: Higher lines, higher poverty. Method matters too. One camp takes an old line and adjusts it for inflation. The other reconstructs the line from spending patterns in the new survey. Both have limitations, and they are answering different questions.
Published - November 17, 2026 01:07 am IST

briefs.headline: Rupee rises 31 paise to 93.63 against U.S. dollar in early trade
briefs.deck: At the interbank forex market, the domestic unit opened at 93.72 against the greenback and gained ground to touch 93.63, registering a gain of 31 paise over its previous close
briefs.bodyText:
The rupee appreciated 31 paise to 93.63 against the U.S. dollar in early trade on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), supported by a fall in Brent crude oil prices, strong foreign fund inflows and a positive trend in domestic equities.
Forex traders said the fall in Brent crude prices helped ease concerns about rising import bills. Moreover, robust foreign institutional inflows — exceeding $8 billion into Indian equities so far this month — and a broad rally in domestic stock benchmarks enthused investors.
At the interbank forex market, the domestic unit opened at 93.72 against the greenback and gained ground to touch 93.63, registering a gain of 31 paise over its previous close.
On Monday (November 16), the rupee appreciated by 25 paise to close at 93.94 against the U.S. dollar.
"We expect the rupee to trade with a positive bias on easing inflation concerns amid softening crude oil prices and strength in the domestic markets. FII inflows and easing concerns over large-scale attacks between the U.S. and Iran may also support the rupee. However, strength in the dollar and a surge in U.S. Treasury yields my cap sharp upside," Anuj Choudhary, Research Analyst, Mirae Asset Sharekhan, said.
Meanwhile, the dollar index, which gauges the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was at 103.50, higher by 0.04%.
Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading 0.79% lower at $91.71 per barrel in futures trade.
Brent crude oil prices have extended their sharp downward slide driven primarily by growing fears of a global supply surplus, with the International Energy Agency projecting a Q4 surplus of roughly 2 million barrels per day as West Asia crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz recover faster than expected, alongside signs of weakening Chinese demand, said Anil Kumar Bhansali, Head of Treasury and Executive Director, Finrex Treasury Advisors LLP.
On the domestic equity market front, the Sensex advanced 108.83 points to 82,184.33 in early trade, while the Nifty was up 31.90 points at 25,325.75.
Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) bought equities worth ₹4,864.68 crore on Monday (November 16), according to exchange data.

briefs.headline: Jimmy Tata backs Tata Sons listing, accuses Noel of ‘back-door takeover’
briefs.deck: He urged the RBI to enforce strict listing timelines and prevent any breakup of the group, while calling on the government and Charity Commissioner to safeguard the trusts’ founding objectives.
briefs.bodyText:
Amid an intensifying power struggle within the Tata Group, Jimmy Naval Tata, 85, younger brother of late Ratan Tata, has thrown his weight behind the listing of Tata Sons, accusing Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata of attempting a “back-door takeover” of the holding company by inducting family members into key trusts.
In a strongly worded communication responding to queries from a Tata stalwart, believed to be Tata Trusts trustee Vijay Singh, Mr. Jimmy Tata alleged that the composition of the trusts was being altered to consolidate family control over Tata Sons.
“In recent time the trusts are being filled with family members of the present Tata Trust Chairman, [Noel Tata] thereby securing a degree of control over Tata Sons that was never the settlors’ intention,” he said.
“It is entirely inappropriate for more than one family member to serve on a given trust; doing so effectively confers ownership rights over the trusts’ significant shareholding in Tata Sons at no consideration whatsoever. Such an arrangement is untenable and amounts to a back-door takeover of Tata Sons,” he added.
Mr. Jimmy Tata, a trustee of several Tata Trusts, said the Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) and Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) were established by their respective founders, who had no children, to serve the larger public interest.
“The trusts were established for the benefit of the Indian people—as laid out in the objects of the trusts (alleviation of poverty and safeguarding Indian culture)—and the trustees were custodians of public trusts that can never be dissolved, unlike private family trusts,” he said, adding that Mr. JRD Tata and his father, Mr. Naval Tata, were conscious of this responsibility.
Backing Tata Sons Chairman N. Chandrasekaran, Mr. Jimmy Tata credited him with turning around heavily indebted group companies, delivering record earnings and dividend payouts exceeding 6,500%, including to Tata Sons shareholders.
Despite overwhelming support for Mr. Chandrasekaran, including a 4-1 vote on the Tata Sons board and a unanimous Tata Trusts resolution, Mr. Noel allegedly sought to block him by invoking veto provisions in the amended Articles of Association without offering justification.
“These developments make the listing of Tata Sons, as mandated by the RBI, all the more critical,” he said.
According to Mr. Jimmy Tata, listing would end the group’s “pervasive culture of secrecy”, strengthen statutory accountability and necessitate changes to the Articles of Association. He also cited the successful public listing of TCS under Ratan Tata as evidence of its benefits.
Rejecting Mr. Noel’s proposed restructuring, he warned that breaking up Tata Sons into smaller entities to circumvent RBI listing requirements would be “deeply damaging and contrary to public and shareholder interests”.
He urged the RBI to enforce strict listing timelines and prevent any breakup of the group, while calling on the government and Charity Commissioner to safeguard the trusts’ founding objectives.
Mr. Jimmy Tata also blamed amendments to the Articles of Association around 2013-14 for concentrating power in the hands of the Tata Trusts chairman. The changes, he alleged, introduced “unnatural, dictatorial veto powers” and the right to nominate directors, undermining collective board authority.
He further questioned the four-year tenure limit imposed on certain trustees while others remained exempt, alleging that dissenting trustees were being marginalised. He cited Mr. Venu Srinivasan, whose term expires in December, and Mr. Vijay Singh as examples.
Contrasting the present leadership with the group’s earlier tradition of appointing independent trustees and nurturing professional talent, Mr. Jimmy Tata named Nani Palkhivala, Gautam Sarabhai, Homi Sethna and Homi Bhabha among past trustees, and Sumant Moolgaokar, Darbari Seth, Xerxes Desai and Rusi Mody among its celebrated executives.

briefs.headline: Export duty on diesel hiked ₹2.5/litre, ATF ₹1.5/litre, petrol remains nil
briefs.deck: The hike in diesel levy assumes added significance as India looks to further up their exports of the vehicular fuel to Europe amid a global supply crunch.
briefs.bodyText:
The government late Monday (November 16, 2026) hiked the export duty on diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) by ₹2.5 per litre and ₹1.5 per litre, whilst keeping the levy on export of petrol unchanged at nil.
Duty rates on petrol and diesel meant for domestic consumption remain unchanged.
The hike in diesel levy assumes added significance as India looks to further up their exports of the vehicular fuel to Europe amid a global supply crunch.
In the upcoming fortnight, diesel exports would draw a levy of ₹14 per litre compared to ₹11.5 per litre mandated for the previous fortnight.
ATF exports would draw a levy of ₹12.5 per litre against ₹11 per litre.
There would be no levies on export of petrol.
The government has been conducting a fortnightly review of export levies since March 27, in the backdrop of the conflict in West Asia. These are done based on the average international benchmark prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF observed since the previous review.
This is to ensure the domestic availability of retail fuels by disincentivising exports.

briefs.headline: Oil prices fall as rising supply outweighs Middle East tensions
briefs.deck: On Tuesday, oil prices dropped slightly as expectations of a global supply surplus gained traction. Analysts observed that geopolitical tensions in the Middle East are now having a diminished impact on pricing. According to the International Energy Agency, there is an anticipated surplus for the last quarter of the year.
briefs.bodyText:
Oil prices plunged marginally on Tuesday, with the prospect of a global supply surplus taking precedence over concerns about attacks on oil tankers in the Middle East. The possibility of rising supplies has weighed on the market even as tensions continue to threaten energy infrastructure and shipping routes in the region.
WTI crude was down 48 cents, or 0.56%, at $85.24, while Brent crude declined 57 cents, or 0.62%, to $91.87. Prices were quoted with a 10-minute delay.
Earlier on Friday, the International Energy Agency said that global oil market would move back into surplus in the fourth quarter of this year. The agency attributed this outlook to Middle East exports recovering at a faster pace than global oil demand, despite attacks on shipping.
However, the security situation in the region remains a concern. Attacks on energy infrastructure and vessels in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz have continued, keeping uncertainty around a major global oil-export route.
Though, geopolitical concerns are still present, they no longer having as much influence on prices as the supply outlook.
Meanwhile, OPEC held a virtual meeting on Monday to discuss its assessment of members' maximum sustainable production capacity. 
The review is an important exercise as it will help establish OPEC+ production quotas for 2027 and subsequent years.
The broader OPEC+ alliance, which also includes oil-producing countries led by Russia, is set to meet on November 29. The meeting will focus on deciding the group's oil output policy for 2027.
In another development, US crude inventories held in the Strategic Petroleum Reserve declined to 276.4 million barrels last week, marking their lowest level since August 1982, according to Department of Energy data.
The latest reduction is part of an agreement by the US to release 172 million barrels of oil from the reserve.

briefs.headline: Videocon insolvency likely to be delayed
briefs.deck: The Supreme Court has ruled that the decision on the haircut for Twinstar Technologies' resolution plan rests with the Committee of Creditors. This ruling has led to further delays in the insolvency proceedings for the Videocon group, initiated in June 2018.
briefs.bodyText:
New Delhi: The 
Supreme Court
 on Monday said that a decision regarding the extent of the haircut falls within the domain of the Committee of Creditors (CoC), whose exercise of commercial wisdom is non-justiciable, while upholding NCLAT's decision to send Twinstar Technologies' Rs 2,962 crore resolution plan for Videocon group back to the creditors for reconsideration.
This means the insolvency proceedings of Videocon, which started in June 2018, are likely to be further delayed. A bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe upheld the NCLAT decision on multiple grounds, including that the resolution plan did not comply with Section 30(2)(b) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC). The bench, however, rejected the promoter's plea on the issue of the haircut, which is around 96%.
"We wish to clarify that the matter pertains to Twin Star Technologies and the proceedings relating to its resolution plan for Videocon Industries. The said matter does not pertain to Vedanta and Vedanta is not a party to the proceedings," said Vedanta release.
In 2021, National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) held that out of admitted claims of Rs 64,839 crore, the plan offered Rs 2,962 crore, resulting in a haircut of 95.8%, and that the operational creditors would receive 0.7% of their admitted claims.

briefs.headline: Samsung, Xiaomi raise phone prices by up to Rs 4,000

briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: 
Samsung
 and 
Xiaomi
 have raised smartphone prices by up to Rs 4,000 after a weak Diwali season. Samsung's Galaxy A07 5G, already above Rs 20,000, is now Rs 2,000 costlier at Rs 22,999. Xiaomi's entry-level Redmi A7 has gone from Rs 12,999 to Rs 14,999.
The revisions, effective Nov 16, range from Rs 1,000 to Rs 4,000 across select Samsung Galaxy A- and F-series and Xiaomi Redmi models. Samsung's increases were as high as nearly 10%, while Xiaomi's reached nearly 19%.
Vivo
 is also expected to raise prices, with its entry-level Y11 5G said to go up from Rs 18,999 to Rs 21,999. Vivo's website continued to display the earlier prices at the time of publication. Queries sent to Vivo and Xiaomi went unanswered.

CyberMedia Research recorded a 94% year-on-year drop in shipments below Rs 7,000 in the Sept quarter and a 42% fall in the Rs 7,000-24,999 range. Shipments below Rs 20,000 fell 47% year on year in the Sept quarter.

stories.headline: IND vs NZ Tests: We will play four fast bowlers for sure, says Gill
stories.deck: Gill explained the rationale behind having a hit-the-deck bowler and pointed out how New Zealand conditions can make the job difficult for fast bowlers, particularly once the Kookaburra ball gets older and loses its potency
stories.bodyText:
India captain Shubman Gill on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) said the team will "for sure" play four fast bowlers in the upcoming Test series against New Zealand and rejected concerns surrounding wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant's form and fitness.
"We will be playing four fast bowlers for sure," Gill declared ahead of the two-match series, which gets underway in Wellington from Thursday (November 19, 2026).
"All our fast bowlers have done well, and it is a good headache to have," he said, referring to the superb performance by a young pace attack in the recent ODI series, which India won 3-1.
The attack will be bolstered by the return of senior pro Jasprit Bumrah. From the white-ball squad, the impressive Gurnoor Brar has been retained at the expense of spinner Kuldeep Yadav.
"We want four fast bowlers but don't know which ones (will play). From day three, we have seen that the pitch gets flat, and we need someone who can hit the deck," Gill said.
The skipper also backed Pant, who has been battling fitness issues.
"There is no dilemma on Rishabh Pant. He has played 50 Tests; he has scored across the globe. He is a wicket-keeper who has a hundred in Australia," Gill said.
Akash Deep and Prasidh Krishna are expected to be part of the pace combination, while Anshul Kamboj has attracted considerable attention from head coach Gautam Gambhir and bowling coach Morne Morkel during the team's preparations.
Gill indicated that the team management is also looking at Akash and Kamboj as potential lower-order contributors, with the possibility of playing seven specialist batters and relying on the two pacers at No. 8 and No. 9.
"We plan to play with seven proper batters and eight and nine, we need to check. Akash and Anshul both can bat. Nitish (Kumar Reddy) too can bat," he said.
Gill explained the rationale behind having a hit-the-deck bowler and pointed out how New Zealand conditions can make the job difficult for fast bowlers, particularly once the Kookaburra ball gets older and loses its potency.
The two tall Indian pacers who fit into that particular description are Prasidh and Brar, although the latter's inclusion in the final XI remains uncertain.
Gill also spoke about the challenges posed by the strong winds in Wellington, which can take a considerable toll on fast bowlers.
"The wind here affects bowlers more than batters. If a fast bowler bowls against the wind, it takes a lot out of him. Hence, we need to check what kind of combinations we should be playing," he said.
The Indian captain believes that a Test match in New Zealand needs to be approached in two distinct phases, with the conditions and nature of the pitch changing considerably as the game progresses.
"We should divide the Test in two parts. First two days and last three days, which is different. Hence, we need someone who will hit the deck. We will go with seven specialist batters," Gill said.
India has also prioritised the two-match Test series in their preparations, pulling players out of the ODI assignments to give them adequate time to acclimatise and prepare for the longer format.
"If we win these two Tests, there is a very good chance of playing the WTC final. Hence, we pulled out all players from ODIs to give them the best chance of preparation," Gill said.
India's immediate objective will be to negotiate the early movement on offer before making the most of what are traditionally flatter surfaces as the match progresses.
